pointers.shared: Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

purpose.is: The watcher is the one process per bearings tier that proves the owner's input has a live consumer end to end, and the lamp is that proof made visible.

It replaces the old wait loop (tools/bearings/scripts/bearings.sh wait, which typed every owner line into one agent pane) with a supervised unit that moves the owner's answers and messages from the page into the intake nodes and acks each one.
purpose.is-not: It is not a monitor of agents, not a scheduler, and never an LLM; it holds a lease, tails a stream, calls two gRPC methods and heartbeats.
purpose.why: Card C32 was posted on 2026-10-14 while no wait loop belonged to the posting session; the owner answered at 03:31Z and nothing delivered it for 40 minutes (HANDOFF.md, defect found ~04:10Z). The system fix ruled there: a card cannot go up unwatched, and the Controls screen shows the watcher as a lamp.
purpose.decisions: D12 system lane (C40), D08 every system process its own supervised unit (C46), D21 push (C52), comms C58; V16 small file protocol with idempotent ids and a consumed set; K03 no agent polls; T06 lease with heartbeat, generation and compare-and-swap.

record.field: the page name from tools/bearings/config/bearings.json tiers, for example coq-stable or coq-dev-WO-20261014-ab12
coq-watcher@<page>.service, the systemd user unit instance that started

input.text: The input is the unit start itself: systemd starts the instance, the binary writes unit.start as its first record and the traversal begins. No other record starts this node.

record.field: name watcher/<page>, token, generation, expiry (from N-02)
alive, grace or dead (the lamp colour is a pure function of this)
true when the tier's page service answered GET /health within the last beat
true when the last Store.Put of this record committed
the highest store seq of an owner answer or message this watcher has handed to N-29 or N-30 and acked

output.text: watcher.alive is an upsert keyed on watcher/<page> (one row per tier, compare-and-swap on version), rewritten every heartbeat. It is the lock with heartbeat the DAG names: the lease in N-02 is the lock, this record is the heartbeat and the lamp. N-28 reads it before posting a card; N-42 draws it.

record.field: UTC of the last heartbeat seen
lease expired, unit exited unclean, or page unreachable past the bound

output.text: watcher.dead is written by the Go service's stall tick (N-12 shape, same clock) when a lease expires without a release, so a watcher that dies silently still produces a record and an alert; the watcher never has to be alive to report its own death.

mechanism.where: A small Go binary in the same module as the control plane (D01, D09 small cut): package internal/owner/watcher, command coq-watcher. It runs as the owner user on the WSL host (D22), as the systemd user unit instance coq-watcher@<page>.service rendered from tools/bearings/units/coq-watcher@.service.
mechanism.step: On start, read tools/bearings/config/bearings.json through the same loader as the page service, resolve the tier and page name, and write unit.start 100.

Acquire the lease watcher/<page> from N-02 with ttl 15 s and holder <unit>:<pid>. A refused lease (another live holder) means a second watcher for one tier: write watcher.refused 409 naming the holder and exit 3, so systemd does not restart it in a loop (RestartPreventExitStatus=3). This is the "one wait per page, or events are delivered twice" rule of tools/bearings/AGENTS.md made into a lease.

Subscribe to the store stream (N-31's gRPC Push.Subscribe with filter tier=<tier>, kinds owner.answer and owner.message, since_seq = the delivered_seq of the last watcher.alive for this page, or 0). This is the consumed set of V16 as a seq watermark instead of delivered.json.

For every owner.answer record, call Intake.Answer (N-29) with the lease token as the fencing token; for every owner.message, call Inbox.Message (N-30) the same way. Both calls are idempotent on the record id, so a repeated delivery after a crash is a no-op with the same reply. On success, advance delivered_seq.

Every 5 s: renew the lease (a third of its ttl, T06), probe GET /health of the tier's page service on loopback with a 2 s timeout, and upsert watcher.alive with state alive, page_ok, store_ok and delivered_seq. The record's version is the compare-and-swap guard; a 409 means another watcher wrote it, which is the lease having been lost (step 7).
On SIGTERM: release the lease, write watcher.down 100 with reason stop, exit 0. The lamp goes grey, not red, because a clean stop is not a death.

On a lease renew that fails with a generation mismatch or on a 409 from step 5: this process no longer holds the lease (a newer generation exists). Write watcher.down 500 with reason fenced and exit 1; systemd restarts it and step 2 decides whether it may run.
mechanism.text: Why a lease and not a pid file: the old wait.lock.json (tools/bearings/scripts/wait.mjs breadcrumb 2026-10-14) was a pid plus a grace window, checked by the server on every poll; it could not say whether the holder was the one consuming this tier's input, and a SIGKILLed holder left a dead pid that read as not alive only by luck. A lease with a generation says exactly one holder consumes, and expiry is the system's clock, not the reader's.

Why the watcher is its own unit and not a goroutine of the page service: the page service restarts on every promotion (N-48) and on every upgrade; the owner's intake must not stop when the page restarts (bearings-stable-is-the-only-always-on-monitor rule), and a card on the page must stay watched through a page restart. Two units, two lifetimes.

Why the watcher does not read the page's files: the page service (N-32) writes the owner's answer or message to the store first (through N-29 and N-30 directly, in the same request) and only then acks the browser; the watcher's stream subscription is the second consumer that proves the path and advances the watermark. If the page service's direct call fails, the record is still in the store as owner.answer or owner.message with no ruling or ack, and the watcher's pass through step 4 delivers it. That is the level-triggered safety net of D21 and T03 applied to the owner's words.

unit.name: coq-watcher@.service
unit.line: [Unit] Description=coq bearings watcher for %i; Wants=coq.service; After=coq.service network-online.target; StartLimitIntervalSec=0

[Service] Type=simple; ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/coq-watcher --page %i; Restart=always; RestartSec=2; RestartPreventExitStatus=3; MemoryMax=128M; Environment=COQ_STATE=%h/.local/state/coq/coq-jev-herdr-plugin

start.text: The stable instance is enabled once by the install script (systemctl --user enable --now coq-watcher@coq-stable) and loginctl enable-linger makes it start at boot with no login and no agent. uat and dev instances are started by the tier promotion node (N-48) when it brings a tier up and stopped when it tears the tier down; a seat never starts one.

Assumption, recorded: systemd runs in this WSL distribution (wsl.conf [boot] systemd=true). The check in the checklist proves it; if it is false, the fallback is a supervisor unit in Podman, and that is a ticket, not a hand start.

wait.fallback: retry 3 times 2 s apart, then watcher.refused 409 or watcher.down 500 with reason store, exit 1; systemd restarts after RestartSec
reconnect with the same since_seq, 3 times with 2, 4, 8 s backoff, then exit 1 and let systemd restart; the lease is released first so a fresh instance can take it

retry 3 times (2, 4, 8 s); then write delivery.failed 500 with the record id and keep going with the next record, because one bad record must not freeze the owner's channel; the failed record is picked up on the next pass since delivered_seq does not advance past it

page_ok=false in the next watcher.alive; three misses in a row set state grace, then the alive record still goes up (the page being down is the page's own alert, N-32 page.stale), the watcher keeps consuming
store_ok=false, retry next beat; two missed beats inside the lease ttl are tolerated (15 s ttl, 5 s beat); the third miss expires the lease and the stall tick writes watcher.dead
forced exit; the lease expires by ttl

waits.no-cog: The cog that could stall this node is the watcher itself being absent. The timeout is the lease ttl; the fallback is the stall tick writing watcher.dead, systemd restarting the unit, N-28 holding cards with 423 until a lamp is back, and the alert reaching the owner through N-41 and, once live, N-52.

retries.rule: Every automated step above retries up to 3 times with backoff, then recovers (exit for systemd, or skip and report) and writes a record that names what failed. Nothing loops without a bound and nothing fails silently.

systemd Restart=always with RestartSec=2 is the fourth and later attempt; the record trail shows each start as unit.start, so a crash loop is countable on the health line (N-06) and becomes an unhealthy alert after 3 starts in 5 minutes, which is an owner-acts code and a card from N-28 (which needs a watcher; see the fallback chain in the waits section).

many-agents-at-once.readers: Any number of seats read this volume at once; it is one file with stable anchors and nothing in it is edited at run time.
many-agents-at-once.workers: Build tickets cut from this node touch internal/owner/watcher, tools/bearings/units/coq-watcher@.service and tools/bearings/bin/install-units.sh and nothing else; N-32 and N-34 own different files, so three authors ship in parallel without a file clash (one file, one in-flight ticket).

collision.what: two watcher instances for one tier

many-agents-at-once.collision: Only one holds the lease watcher/<page>; the second gets lease.refused from N-02, writes watcher.refused 409 and exits 3. If the first dies, its lease expires by ttl (15 s) and the next start takes it with generation plus one; a late write from the old holder carries the old token and is refused by N-01 as 409, so it can never advance delivered_seq backwards.

collision.what: the page service and the watcher both deliver the same owner.answer

many-agents-at-once.collision: Intake.Answer is idempotent on the record id and rules once by compare-and-swap (N-29); the second call returns the existing ruling. The same holds for Inbox.Message. Double delivery is a no-op by design, never a double effect.

collision.what: a dev or uat watcher sees its page stop

many-agents-at-once.collision: Its page.down 100 (reason idle) is a record for that tier only; the architect digest lane (N-30) is fed by the stable watcher alone, so a throwaway tier's STOPPED never wakes the architect (nodes/N-32/spec.xml#tier-rules, rule wake-only-stable).
Each tier has its own lease name, its own watermark and its own units; a dev tier can never consume the stable page's records because the subscription filter carries the tier.

collision.what: N-28 reads the lamp while it is being rewritten

many-agents-at-once.collision: The read is of the last committed version; a card post checks state alive and beat within 15 s; a torn read is impossible because the store commits whole records.
many-agents-at-once.test: tests run two watcher binaries against one tier with a fake clock (scheduler/internal/testkit): exactly one alive record per beat, the loser exits 3, a kill of the winner yields watcher.dead within one ttl and a new generation within one RestartSec.

look.rule: The lamp is drawn in the Factorio lamp language on the Controls screen (N-42), the bearings page strip (N-32) and the alerts screen (N-41): a round lamp sprite in original art, lit green for alive, amber for grace, red for dead, unlit grey for a clean stop or no unit. Values only from the art inventory section 4.3: green #2BE327, red #DA4535, amber from the orange accent #FAA838, caption text #FFE6C0; no Wube or BiusArt pixel.
look.check: A screenshot of each state on the dev tier, read by the architect and sent to the owner before the promotion card (screenshot-every-page-change), is the proof; the four states are produced by the test harness, not by waiting for a real death.

permissions.runs-as: the owner user, no sudo, MemoryMax 128M
permissions.may: acquire and renew the lease watcher/<page>; subscribe to records of its tier; call Intake.Answer and Inbox.Message with its fencing token; upsert watcher.alive for its page; read server.json of its tier for the loopback port
permissions.may-not: post cards, write rulings, reply to the owner, read another tier, call herdr, or touch the repository
permissions.socket: gRPC over the unix socket ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/coq/control.sock, mode 0600 (scheduler.proto h-proto-sockets); no TCP

alert.to: N-41 alerts, N-52 phone push when live

alert.when: 3 unit.start in 5 min for one page
alert.to: N-06 unhealthy, then N-28 card when a lamp is back

monitoring.self-check: The system reports on itself: the lamp is computed by the reader from beat age, so a frozen writer shows as grace then dead with no human noticing it first (L08 finding 5).

runbook.op: tools/bearings/bin/install-units.sh (idempotent): copies unit templates, systemctl --user daemon-reload, enables coq-watcher@coq-stable, prints the state. Run once per machine by the bring-up ticket, never by a seat during a run.
systemctl --user status coq-watcher@coq-stable; coq owner lamp --page coq-stable (prints the last watcher.alive and its age)
systemctl --user stop coq-watcher@<page>; stable is never stopped by hand (bearings-stable-is-the-only-always-on-monitor); N-48 stops dev and uat instances

If a lease is wedged (holder dead, ttl not expiring because the clock node is down): coq lease break watcher/<page> is owner-only and one time (shared/seat-contract.xml#break-glass); the record names who and why.
tools/bearings/bin/cleanup-tier.sh <page> --dry-run, then --yes; tools/bearings/bin/cleanup-journal.sh; tools/bearings/bin/install-units.sh --remove on decommission
runbook.cost: One more process per tier (about 10 MB), five small store writes a minute per tier, and a 15 s window in which a dead watcher still reads alive.
